International Baccalaureate = a two-year diploma programme recognised by universities worldwide
literacy = the ability to read and write at a functional level
numeracy = the ability to use numbers in everyday and work situations
information literacy = the skills needed to find, judge and use information, including online
admission requirements = the grades or qualifications needed to join a course
mock exam = a practice exam taken under real conditions before the official one
resit = a second attempt at an exam after a fail or a low grade
coursework = assessed work completed during a course rather than in a final exam
oral exam = a spoken test of knowledge or language
written examination = a formal test answered on paper or on screen
continuous assessment = grading based on work throughout the course, not one final paper
formative assessment = checking progress to improve learning, often without a final grade
summative assessment = a test or task that measures what has been learnt at the end of a unit
pass mark = the lowest score needed to succeed in a test
grade boundary = the score at which one grade changes to the next
academic transcript = an official record of modules and grades from an institution
credit points = units that measure the workload of a course or module
invigilator = a person who supervises an exam to prevent cheating
exam board = the organisation that sets and marks a public exam
marking criteria = the stated standards used to award marks
